text: For Heidegger, a hammer being used transparently in skilled work — without becoming an object of explicit attention — exemplifies the mode of being he calls:
explanation: Transparent, absorbed use of equipment exemplifies the ready-to-hand (Zuhandenheit). Present-at-hand (Vorhandenheit) is the contrasting mode that arises when a tool breaks down and becomes a mere object; being-in-itself is Sartre's category for things; and the natural attitude belongs to Husserl's method.
